assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsars opened a new observational window on compact stars and enabled precise tests of gravity and neutron-star physics. This is a landmark discovery.
assessment.attribution: Bell's detection and recognition of the anomalous signals were central. A complete historical account must also consider the wider discovery team and the division of credit.
assessment.maturity: Pulsars have been studied for decades across many systems and observing methods; their existence and scientific importance are firmly established.
uncertainties: The discovery's historical credit is contested, and this candidate names Bell alone.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The holographic principle and AdS/CFT have reshaped quantum field theory and quantum gravity, with durable influence across theoretical physics.
assessment.attribution: These names represent foundational steps in the principle and its concrete realization, though the intellectual development spans a wider community.
assessment.maturity: The duality has generated extensive results and tests within theory, but its connection to the physical universe remains unconfirmed.
uncertainties: The long-term status of string-theoretic duality as a description of nature is unknown; overlapping nominations make the appropriate scope of recognition difficult to define.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: SASE made intense, coherent X-ray pulses practical and enabled experiments on matter at ultrafast timescales and atomic length scales. This is a major experimental tool.
assessment.attribution: The three credited physicists made important contributions to the concept and its realization; the full achievement also depended on substantial accelerator and facility teams.
assessment.maturity: Operating XFEL facilities have established the method's scientific reach over many years.
uncertainties: The balance of credit among the conceptual work, accelerator development, and facility teams needs careful assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Higgs-boson discovery completed a central part of the Standard Model and confirmed a mechanism with broad consequences for particle physics.
assessment.attribution: These leaders represent the experimental collaborations, but the discovery depended on thousands of people and the combined ATLAS and CMS results.
assessment.maturity: The discovery has been independently confirmed, and subsequent measurements have substantially characterized the particle.
uncertainties: Selecting a few individuals to represent two large collaborations remains a difficult attribution judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Horizon-scale imaging transformed black holes from theoretical and indirect objects into directly imaged structures and demonstrated a remarkable new capability in radio astronomy.
assessment.attribution: The named scientists provided important scientific and technical leadership, while the image depended on a large international collaboration.
assessment.maturity: The result has been followed by additional observations and images; the instrument and analysis methods have proven robust.
uncertainties: The extent to which the imaging itself yields a lasting advance in fundamental physics, beyond its extraordinary observational achievement, remains open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detecting high-energy neutrinos from cosmic sources opened a new channel on the universe and established neutrino astronomy as a field.
assessment.attribution: Halzen's scientific leadership and Spiering's major role in building the field and detector effort are substantial; the result is also the work of a large collaboration.
assessment.maturity: The astrophysical neutrino flux is established, with observations from multiple sources strengthening the case for this new astronomy.
uncertainties: Credit for the discovery is distributed across a large detector collaboration and a sequence of observations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The magnetar picture identified an important class of neutron stars and explained energetic phenomena through magnetic fields far beyond those accessible in the laboratory.
assessment.attribution: The candidate spans theoretical prediction and observational confirmation, a sensible pairing for this achievement.
assessment.maturity: Many observations support magnetars and their extreme-field interpretation, though individual emission mechanisms remain under study.
uncertainties: The boundary between magnetars and other neutron-star populations, and the details of their activity, remain active research questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices provide a controlled platform for exploring strongly correlated matter and quantum many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: The proposed names cover key theoretical and experimental advances, but the candidate combines work by several groups and the full credited list is unusually broad.
assessment.maturity: The platform is mature and has produced extensive results; its value as a simulator of particular condensed-matter systems continues to be assessed.
uncertainties: How reliably these experiments reproduce the hardest regimes of real materials remains a scientific question.
